title: Returning an Online Order at a Shop

cover.alt: A customer shows an online order confirmation while returning a boxed item to a shop assistant.

blocks.title: Returning an Online Order at a Shop
paragraphs: You ordered something online, but it arrived wrong or broken. Now you need to go to the shop and return it. You will learn how to bring the right evidence, explain the problem clearly, ask about a refund or exchange, and check what happens to your money. These phrases work in most shops.

blocks.title: Before You Start
blocks.intro: Think about these questions before you read.

items.prompt: Have you ever returned something to a shop? What did you bring with you?
items.explanation: What do you think is the hardest part of returning something in a foreign language?

items.prompt: What information do you think a shop assistant needs before they can help you?

blocks.title: Bringing Your Order Evidence
paragraphs: Before you go to the shop, collect your evidence. You need the order confirmation email or a printed order number. You also need the original packaging if you still have it, and the item itself. Many shops also ask for the card or account you used to pay.

For example, Yuki received a jacket in the wrong size. She took her phone to the shop and showed the assistant her order confirmation email. The assistant scanned the order number immediately. Without that number, the return would have taken much longer. Always check the shop's own return policy for the exact documents they need.

images.alt: The same customer and assistant check the box, packaging, order confirmation, and payment card.

items.prompt: Yuki wanted to return a jacket. What did she show the shop assistant?
choices: A handwritten note with the price
A photo of the jacket on the website
items.explanation:
Yuki showed her order confirmation email on her phone. The assistant scanned the order number from it straight away.

When you return something, do you usually keep the confirmation email or delete it? What will you do differently now?

blocks.title: Explaining the Problem Clearly
paragraphs: Keep your explanation short and specific. Say what is wrong, not just that you are unhappy. Use these patterns: "The item is damaged.", "The colour is different from the website.", "I received the wrong size.", or "It stopped working after one use."

For example, Carlos opened his headphones and found the left side had no sound. He said to the assistant, "I bought these online and the left side doesn't work. I only used them once." That one clear sentence gave the assistant everything needed to start the return. Avoid long stories; one or two sentences are enough.

items.prompt: Carlos's headphones had a problem. Which sentence best describes what he said to the assistant?
items.answer: "The left side doesn't work and I only used them once."
choices: "I don't like these headphones at all."
"The left side doesn't work and I only used them once."
"These cost a lot of money and I am very unhappy."
"Can you check if these are broken?"
items.explanation:
Carlos gave a short, specific description: what was wrong and for how long he had used the item. That is the most useful information for the assistant.

Think of something you own that broke or arrived damaged. How would you describe the problem in one or two English sentences?

blocks.title: Asking About a Refund or Exchange
paragraphs: Once you have explained the problem, ask what options are available. Two simple questions cover most situations: "Is it possible to get a refund?" and "Can I exchange this for the correct size?" If you are not sure which you prefer, ask: "What are my options?"

Always ask how the money is returned. Say: "Will the refund go back to my original payment method?" or "How long does the refund usually take?" Shops handle this differently, so it is important to ask. The assistant cannot always give you an instant answer, but asking puts the information in front of you.

items.prompt: You want a refund but you are not sure what options the shop offers. Which question is the best first step?
items.explanation:
Asking "What are my options?" is polite and open. It lets the assistant explain everything that is available without making the conversation difficult.

Imagine the shop says a refund is not possible but an exchange is. How would you respond politely in English?

rows.meaning: Explain exactly what was wrong with the order.
rows.example: I ordered this online, but I received the wrong size.

rows.term: Is it possible to get a refund?
rows.meaning: Ask politely whether you can get your money back.
rows.example: The item is damaged. Is it possible to get a refund?

rows.term: Can I exchange this for the correct size?
rows.meaning: Ask to replace the item instead of getting money back.
rows.example: This jacket is too small. Can I exchange this for the correct size?

rows.term: Will the refund go back to my original payment method?
rows.meaning: Check where the returned money will be sent.
rows.example: Will the refund go back to my original payment method?

blocks.title: Situation
paragraphs: Yuki is at the returns desk with the item, its packaging, and her order confirmation. The assistant asks what happened and whether she wants a refund or an exchange.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: Hello. I'd like to return this jacket, please. I ordered it online and it arrived in the wrong size.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Of course. Do you have your order number or confirmation email?

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: Yes, I have the confirmation email here on my phone.

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Perfect, thank you. Let me scan that. What would you like to do — a refund or an exchange?

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: I'd like an exchange for a medium, please. Do you have it in stock?

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Let me check... yes, we do. I'll get that for you. Would you like to try it on first?

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: Yes, please. Also, if the exchange isn't possible for some reason, is it possible to get a refund instead?

turns.speaker: Assistant
turns.text: Yes, absolutely. If the exchange doesn't work out, we can process a refund to your original payment method.

turns.speaker: Yuki
turns.text: Great, thank you so much for your help.

blocks.title: Your Turn
blocks.intro: Change the situation and practise it in your own words.

items.prompt: Choose one problem: the wrong size, a damaged item, or an item that stopped working. Explain the problem, ask for a refund or exchange, and check the payment method.
items.explanation:
Hello. I'd like to return this, please.

Use two or three phrases from the lesson, then switch roles and change the item.

blocks.title: Final Reflection
paragraphs: Bring your order confirmation email or order number, the item, and the original packaging if you have it. Explain the problem in one or two clear sentences. Ask "Is it possible to get a refund?" or "Can I exchange this?" and use "What are my options?" if you are unsure. Always ask how your money is returned and how long it takes. Every shop has its own return policy, so check the details before you go. Which sentence would help you start your own return clearly?
